rationale: The identified Workload Service Assurance feature is a conventional scheduler mechanism: HCL docs describe critical-job deadlines, promotion, priority/resource allocation, and SLA protection. A separate HCL Workload Automation article discusses AI Data Advisory/anomaly detection in HWA version 10, but does not establish that this particular optional Service Assurance feature uses AI. The feature-specific best call is non-AI; uncertainty about product/version and broader suite applicability makes it weak/forced.
version_scope: No version/date in source record. HCL docs are v10.2.6; HWA 10 AI article is broader suite evidence and is not conflated with the identified optional Service Assurance feature.
issues: Same broader HWA suite has separately documented AI anomaly detection; its inclusion within the identified optional feature is not established.

sources.excerpt: The workload service assurance feature is enabled and disabled by the global option enWorkloadServiceAssurance. It is enabled by default. ... calculates a critical start time ... promoted job is assigned additional operating system resources and its submission is prioritized.
sources.applicability: Official HWA 10.2.6 documentation describes the identified feature's deterministic deadline/priority/resource behavior, not AI.
